findings.observation: Both texts name a contact point and conserve the index sequence beginning with zero, but neither states what that zero-order case means or why the reflected center is dark at ideal contact. The applicability sentence lists thinness, near-normal incidence and unchanged reflection phase without explicitly stating the zero central gap assumed by the geometry. Thus the requested center/contact case is left for a child to infer from the algebra.
findings.scientificReason: At ideal contact there is no extra propagation distance at the center, while the relative reflection reversal remains: the reflected center is dark. The zero-order center is not a finite-radius ring. A residual central gap changes the phase condition and may change center brightness; thinness alone does not guarantee the contact-based radius formula.
